topic: NLP4PBM: process extraction from natural-language text
topic_definition: Stage 1 only uses title and abstract. Judge whether the paper specifically covers NLP for process extraction from natural-language text. Do not turn missing title/abstract evidence into new hard exclusions.
decision_policy: Recommend exclude when any exclusion criterion is clearly triggered or when the title/abstract directly contradicts the core process-extraction fit. Recommend maybe when the paper appears plausibly relevant but decisive details remain unresolved from title/abstract alone. Recommend include only when the observable Stage 1 fit is directly supported and no exclusion criterion is triggered.

criteria.criterion_text: Title/abstract explicitly indicates that the paper specifically covers the use of NLP for process extraction from natural language text.
criteria.criterion_question: Does the title/abstract directly state or clearly imply that the paper specifically uses NLP for process extraction from natural-language text?
criteria.assessment_policy: Prefer UNCLEAR rather than NO when the paper looks process-related but the extraction target is not explicit.

criteria.criterion_text: Observable task signal links natural-language text to process-model or process-representation extraction/construction objectives.
criteria.criterion_question: Does the observable task signal link natural-language text to extraction or construction of a process model, process representation, BPMN/DMN model, or similar process artifact?
criteria.assessment_policy: Entity extraction alone is not automatically enough unless the title/abstract directly ties it to process-model or decision-model construction.

criteria.criterion_text: When the core fit is plausible but title/abstract evidence is incomplete, keep maybe and defer final confirmation to Stage 2 instead of adding new hard exclusions.
criteria.criterion_question: If the core fit is plausible but incomplete from title/abstract alone, is there a clear reason to defer this candidate to Stage 2 rather than exclude it now?
criteria.assessment_policy: Use YES only when there is a plausible positive path that needs full-text confirmation.

criteria.criterion_text: Title/abstract clearly indicates the study is not specifically covering NLP for process extraction from natural language text.
criteria.criterion_question: Does the title/abstract clearly indicate that the study is not specifically about NLP for process extraction from natural-language text?
criteria.assessment_policy: Use YES for direct mismatch, not for generic absence of detail.

criteria.criterion_text: Observable non-target examples from EC.3: NLP for process redesign, matching, or process prediction.
criteria.criterion_question: Does the title/abstract show that the paper is about process redesign, matching, or process prediction rather than process extraction?
criteria.assessment_policy: Use YES only when the non-target task is the paper's explicit focus.

criteria.criterion_text: Observable non-target examples from EC.3: sentiment analysis, works targeting individual labels instead of natural text, or studies on generating natural text from processes.
criteria.criterion_question: Does the title/abstract show a non-target text task such as sentiment analysis, individual-label prediction, or natural-language generation from processes instead of process extraction?
criteria.assessment_policy: Use YES only when the non-target family is directly supported.

criteria.criterion_text: Survey/review papers are excluded when title/abstract clearly indicates secondary research.
criteria.criterion_question: Does the title/abstract clearly indicate that this is a survey, review, or other secondary research article?
criteria.assessment_policy: Use YES only for explicit secondary-research signals.
